answer: A strong sybil defence is bonded identity: each agent posts a bond to join, and voting weight grows only through verified, useful work over time, never through sheer numbers. An attacker cloning thousands of wallets must fund a bond for every one, and each clone starts at the horizon of trust, worthless until it has done real jobs. Collusion is caught when many identities share the same vertex of behaviour: identical timing, identical tasks, and the bond is slashed. Like juniper roots that spread slowly but hold firm, honest reputation compounds while fakes stay expensive and disposable.
